name: Google Workspace (Gmail, Drive, Docs, Sheets, Calendar, Meet)
dataHosting: US default; EU on higher tiers
keyRisks: Data subject to US CLOUD Act. Extensive tracking feeds ad/AI models. Free tier eliminated for orgs. Data export possible but complex. EU hosting only on expensive plans.

name: Gmail (free/personal)
keyRisks: All email scanned for ads/AI. No data residency options. Not GDPR compliant for organisational use. Easy to leave but contacts/history lost.

name: Microsoft 365 (Outlook, OneDrive, Word, Excel, Teams, SharePoint)
keyRisks: UK hosting available but parent co. still US-jurisdicted. Deepest lock-in of any suite. Prices risen ~25% in 3 years. Copilot/AI trains on your data by default.

name: Microsoft Teams
keyRisks: Tightly bundled with M365 — near-impossible to use alternatives. Metadata extensively collected. Requires M365 licence.

name: Slack
keyRisks: Acquired by Salesforce 2021. Data in US. Free tier: 90-day history limit. Paid plans expensive for small orgs. Good data export.

name: Zoom
keyRisks: Updated ToS 2023 allowing AI training on calls. Data routed through US. Low lock-in. Prices increased.

name: WhatsApp (organisational use)
keyRisks: Metadata harvested even with E2E encryption. Owned by Meta. Not suitable for sensitive organisational comms. No group data export.

name: Dropbox
keyRisks: Data in US. Moderate tracking. Reasonable export. Easy to switch. Prices have increased.

name: Salesforce
keyRisks: Extremely deep lock-in. Proprietary data model. Very expensive. Migration is a major project. EU hosting available.

name: HubSpot
keyRisks: Data in US. Freemium hooks you in, prices escalate. Proprietary data model. Tracks website visitors extensively.

name: Canva
keyRisks: Data on US infrastructure. Teams prices increased 300% in 2024. AI features train on content. Templates/brand kits create dependency.

name: Mailchimp
keyRisks: Acquired by Intuit. Free tier severely cut. Data shared across Intuit products. Significant price increases since acquisition.

name: Trello
keyRisks: Owned by Atlassian. Data in US. Free tier limited. Low lock-in — easy to export and switch.

name: Monday.com
keyRisks: Data in US. Expensive per-seat pricing. Moderate lock-in through workflows. Tracks usage for AI.

name: Asana
keyRisks: Data in US. Per-seat pricing. Moderate lock-in. AI features in development. Good data export. Increasingly expensive.

name: WordPress.com (hosted)
keyRisks: Hosted version is US-based. Self-hosted WordPress.org is open source and excellent. Lock-in through proprietary themes/plugins.

name: Squarespace
keyRisks: Data in US. Proprietary — cannot take your site elsewhere. Poor data export. Annual pricing creates lock-in.

name: Wix
keyRisks: Data in US. Highest lock-in of any CMS — virtually impossible to migrate. Aggressive upselling.

name: SurveyMonkey
keyRisks: Data in US. Expensive. Low lock-in (data exportable). Tracks respondent behaviour. Significant price increases.

name: Typeform
keyRisks: Spanish company but US cloud. GDPR compliant. Low lock-in. Expensive per-response pricing.

name: Google Forms
keyRisks: All responses feed Google's data ecosystem. Free but data is harvested. Tied to Google Sheets.

name: Meta (Facebook / Instagram)
keyRisks: Maximum surveillance. Data harvested for ads. Algorithmic control over reach. Community locked in platform.

name: X / Twitter
keyRisks: Under Musk: unpredictable policy changes, API restricted, staff gutted. High continuity risk. Maximum surveillance.

name: LinkedIn
keyRisks: Microsoft-owned. Extensive professional data harvesting. AI training on posts/messages. Network lock-in.

name: Calendly
keyRisks: Data in US. Calendar access is sensitive. Low lock-in. Easy to replace.

name: Eventbrite
keyRisks: Data in US. Attendee data harvested. Transaction fees. Moderate lock-in through event history.

name: Amazon Web Services
keyRisks: UK hosting available but Amazon is US-jurisdicted. Deep lock-in through proprietary services. CLOUD Act applies.

name: Microsoft Outlook
dataHosting: UK/EU residency available within Microsoft 365; consumer service is provider-managed
keyRisks: US-jurisdicted provider. Organisational mail can use UK/EU Microsoft 365 data residency, but account, telemetry and support data may cross regions. Standards-based email reduces technical lock-in, while deep Microsoft ecosystem integration creates workflow lock-in.

name: Google Drive
dataHosting: US/global infrastructure; regional controls available on some Workspace editions
keyRisks: US-jurisdicted provider and extensive account/activity telemetry. Export is available, but native Docs/Sheets formats and Workspace workflows create soft lock-in.

name: Microsoft OneDrive
dataHosting: UK/EU data residency available within Microsoft 365
keyRisks: US-jurisdicted provider despite regional hosting options. Strong Office/SharePoint/Teams integration makes migration increasingly difficult as organisational workflows deepen.

name: Box
dataHosting: US by default; Box Zones supports UK, EU and other regional storage on higher enterprise plans
keyRisks: US company and US legal jurisdiction remain relevant even with regional Box Zones. Good file portability, but advanced residency/governance capabilities sit on higher-cost enterprise plans.

name: Google Meet
dataHosting: Google global infrastructure; Workspace regional controls apply to some data and editions
keyRisks: US-jurisdicted Google service with substantial account and usage telemetry. Meetings are relatively easy to replace, but integration with Calendar, Gmail and Workspace increases ecosystem dependence.

name: Discord
dataHosting: Provider-managed global cloud; EEA users have Discord Netherlands BV as data controller
keyRisks: US-operated platform with extensive community, message and activity metadata. Discord provides JSON data exports and privacy controls, but migrating whole communities, roles and histories is difficult.

name: Telegram
dataHosting: For UK/EEA users, Telegram states personal data is stored in data centres in the Netherlands
keyRisks: Cloud chats are not end-to-end encrypted by default; only Secret Chats are. Jurisdiction and corporate structure are less straightforward than UK/EU-owned providers, though Telegram states UK/EEA data is stored in the Netherlands.

name: Jira
dataHosting: AWS; paid Cloud plans support UK, EU and other data-residency regions
keyRisks: Deep workflow customisation, Marketplace apps and proprietary issue/project structures create substantial switching costs. Regional hosting is available, but Atlassian remains a multinational cloud provider and migration is a significant project.

name: Smartsheet
dataHosting: US by default; separate EU and Australia regional instances available
keyRisks: US company; even regional instances can involve US access to system/account data. Complex sheets, automations, forms and integrations create growing workflow lock-in and switching cost.

name: Figma
dataHosting: US by default; Enterprise can host key file content in EU, Australia, India or Brazil on AWS
keyRisks: US-jurisdicted proprietary collaborative design platform. EU/localised hosting is Enterprise-only and excludes some metadata. Native collaborative files and organisation libraries create significant workflow lock-in.

name: Adobe Illustrator
dataHosting: Local files possible; Creative Cloud storage and account services are provider-managed
keyRisks: Proprietary AI file format and Creative Cloud ecosystem create strong workflow and licence dependence. Local storage reduces hosting exposure, but Adobe remains a US subscription software provider.

name: Adobe InDesign
dataHosting: Local files possible; Creative Cloud storage and account services are provider-managed
keyRisks: Proprietary INDD workflows, linked assets and Creative Cloud licensing make migration costly. Local files reduce data-hosting dependence but not vendor, format or subscription lock-in.

name: Miro
dataHosting: EU is the default region; US, Australia and Japan regions are also supported
keyRisks: EU data residency is strong, but Miro is a proprietary multinational SaaS platform. Complex boards, integrations and embedded workflows are hard to move cleanly to another product.

name: Mural
keyRisks: US-jurisdicted proprietary collaboration service. Rich boards, templates, facilitation features and integrations create significant workflow lock-in; exports do not reproduce the full interactive workspace.

name: Substack
keyRisks: Audience, publishing, payments and discovery are bundled into one US platform. Subscriber export is possible, but network effects, archives and paid-subscription workflows create meaningful soft lock-in.

name: Medium
dataHosting: AWS and other service providers across multiple countries
keyRisks: US-hosted publishing platform with platform-controlled distribution and product changes. Account data can be exported, but audience, recommendations and publication presence do not transfer cleanly.

name: Constant Contact
keyRisks: US SaaS provider. Contact export is available and the company says it does not sell or rent customers' contacts, but templates, automations, reporting history and integrations create switching work and pricing exposure.

name: Campaign Monitor
keyRisks: Proprietary marketing platform under a US-based parent group. Lists can be exported, but campaign history, automations, templates and integrations create soft lock-in and ongoing per-contact cost exposure.

name: Microsoft Forms
dataHosting: Within Microsoft 365 regional infrastructure, with UK/EU residency options for eligible tenants
keyRisks: US-jurisdicted provider and strong Microsoft 365 integration. Responses can be exported, but identity, Excel, Teams and Power Automate workflows can create wider ecosystem dependence.

name: Doodle
dataHosting: Provider-managed infrastructure with international subprocessors and contractual transfer safeguards
keyRisks: Swiss provider with relatively low functional lock-in, but personal data can be processed internationally through subprocessors. Free/ad-supported usage and integrations add tracking exposure.

name: GoDaddy
keyRisks: US-jurisdicted provider with bundled domains, hosting, email and site-builder products that can accumulate cross-service lock-in. Introductory pricing and renewals can increase cost exposure.

name: Google Cloud Platform
dataHosting: Customer-selectable UK/EU and global cloud regions
keyRisks: Regional hosting can keep workloads in the UK/EU, but Google remains a US provider. Proprietary managed services, IAM and data platforms can create deep architectural lock-in and difficult cost forecasting.

name: Microsoft Azure
dataHosting: Customer-selectable UK/EU and global cloud regions
keyRisks: UK/EU regions are available, but Microsoft remains US-jurisdicted. Managed services, Entra identity, licensing and Microsoft ecosystem integration can produce deep technical and commercial lock-in.
